# Fuse

> Fuse is a .NET tool that keeps a repository's C# solution compiled in memory with Roslyn and gives AI coding agents the compiler errors their edits introduced, the tests those edits can break, and compact build output. It runs through agent hooks and an MCP server, locally, with no telemetry.

Fuse needs the .NET 10 SDK. Install it with `dotnet tool install -g Fuse`, then run `fuse init` in a repository. `fuse init` registers Fuse's hooks with each harness the repository uses (Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI and OpenCode), and the MCP server with VS Code agent mode. After each edit the agent gets only the errors that edit introduced, compared with HEAD, the commit you have checked out. When the agent runs `dotnet test`, only the affected tests run and only failures are printed. Fuse is open source under the Apache-2.0 license.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://fuse.codes/docs/): what Fuse is, the words the documentation uses, and which page answers which question
- [Getting started](https://fuse.codes/docs/getting-started): install Fuse and see what it reports on a sample repository
- [Connect your agent](https://fuse.codes/docs/harnesses): what fuse init writes for each harness, and how an MCP host runs fuse mcp
- [How it works](https://fuse.codes/docs/how-it-works): how Fuse checks an edit, selects tests and runs them, and common questions
- [Limits](https://fuse.codes/docs/limits): what Fuse cannot check, and what to do about it
- [Results](https://fuse.codes/docs/results): measurements on four repositories, with the result file behind each number
- [Commands](https://fuse.codes/docs/commands): every fuse command, its arguments, its output and its exit codes
- [Messages and fixes](https://fuse.codes/docs/messages): every message Fuse prints when it cannot answer, and the fix
- [Troubleshooting](https://fuse.codes/docs/troubleshooting): silent hooks, slow checks, log locations and how to stop the engine
- [Changelog](https://fuse.codes/docs/changelog): what changed in each release, the upgrade steps, and which versions are supported

- [Architecture](https://fuse.codes/docs/architecture): how the code is organized, for contributors and coding agents
